analysis.note: Vocative to the sun as nourisher; the commentary derives the name from nourishing the world.

samasa.vigraha: ekaḥ ṛṣiḥ; bhāṣye: eka eva ṛṣati gacchati

analysis.note: One word, not two; although formally eka+ṛṣi, Śaṅkara glosses it by eka eva ṛṣati gacchati, so the translation follows “sole traverser” rather than simply “one seer.”

verification.detail: compound stem ekarṣi as Pum/Sambodhana/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Vocative; glossed as the restrainer/controller of all.
Vocative; Śaṅkara explains the name by taking in rays, vital breaths, and essences.
Vocative patronymic/substantive: offspring of Prajāpati.
Second-person singular imperative; the commentary glosses the sense as vigamaya, “make go away, remove.”
Accusative plural object of vyūha; the commentary adds svān, “your own.”
Second-person singular imperative; glossed as ekīkuru and, in the unsegmented line, apparently upasaṃhara.
Accusative singular object of samūha; line 2 appears under-segmented around upasaṃharate tejastāpakaṃ, but the intended gloss is clearly “heat-making light.”
Accusative singular relative pronoun agreeing with rūpam and correlated with tat.

Enclitic genitive singular, glossed by tava. Masculine linga is supplied for a checkable subanta analysis according to the masculine solar addressee; the personal-pronoun form itself is not distinct by gender.
Accusative singular, governed by paśyāmi through the relative-correlative construction.
Superlative adjective agreeing with rūpam; glossed as atyantaśobhanam.
Accusative singular correlative to yat, object of paśyāmi.

Enclitic genitive singular; Śaṅkara construes it with tava/ātmanas prasāda, “your own favor.” Masculine linga is supplied for a checkable subanta analysis according to the masculine solar addressee; the personal-pronoun form itself is not distinct by gender.
First-person singular present: “I behold.”

Predicate/head of the relative clause; the commentary locates him in the solar disk and gives traditional derivations of puruṣa.

justifications.decision: Translate as “O Pūṣan (nourisher), O ekarṣi (sole traverser), O Yama (restrainer), O Sūrya, O Prājāpatya (offspring of Prajāpati),” not as unrelated deities or as a separate “one sage.”
options_considered: the names are solar vocatives with commentary-specific etymologies
justifications.chosen: The opening five forms are vocatives to the one solar deity, each rendered by Śaṅkara’s etymological sense.

evidence.quote: he pūṣan! jagataḥ poṣaṇātpūṣā ravistathaika eva ṛṣati gacchati ityekarṣiḥ-- he ekarṣe! tathā sarvasya saṃyamanādyamaḥ-- he yama! tathā raśmīnāṃ prāṇānāṃ rasānāñca svīkaraṇāt sūryaḥ-- he sūrya! prajāpaterapatyaṃ prājāpatyaḥ-- he prājāpatya!
evidence.translation: “O Pūṣan: because he nourishes the world he is Pūṣan, the Sun. Likewise, because he alone moves/goes, he is ekarṣi—O ekarṣi. Likewise, because of restraining all, he is Yama—O Yama. Likewise, because of taking in rays, vital breaths, and essences, he is Sūrya—O Sūrya. The offspring of Prajāpati is Prājāpatya—O Prājāpatya.”

justifications.decision: Take raśmīn as the accusative object of the imperative vyūha, with vyūha in the sense of vigamaya, “make depart/remove,” rather than “arrange” or “marshal.”
justifications.chosen: vyūha raśmīn means “disperse/remove your own rays.”

justifications.decision: Take tejaḥ as neuter accusative singular, the object of samūha; the commentary glosses samūha by ekīkuru and apparently by upasaṃhara, and defines tejas as heat-making light. The transmitted line is under-segmented around upasaṃharate tejastāpakaṃ, so the segmentation is noted rather than silently normalized.
justifications.chosen: samūha tejaḥ means “draw together/withdraw the burning light.”

evidence.translation: “Samūha: make one/collect; withdraw your heat-making light.”

justifications.decision: Render kalyāṇatamam according to the gloss atyantaśobhanam, and construe te as genitive (“of yours/your own”), not as an unrelated dative.
options_considered: the most auspicious/beautiful form of yours, seen by your favor
justifications.chosen: The “form” is the sun’s most auspicious/beautiful form, beheld through his own favor.

evidence.quote: yatte tava rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamam atyantaśobhanaṃ tatte tavātmanaḥ prasādāt paśyāmi
evidence.translation: “That form of yours which is kalyāṇatama, exceedingly beautiful, that I behold through the favor of your own self.”

justifications.decision: Translate puruṣa as “person (puruṣa)” with the solar location supplied by the commentary; Śaṅkara supports the term by person-shapedness and by the traditional “lying in the city” derivation.
options_considered: the person in the solar disk
justifications.chosen: puruṣaḥ is the yonder person in the solar disk, not a generic human being.

evidence.translation: “Who is yonder, situated in the solar disk.”
“He is puruṣa because he has the form of a person.”
“Or he is puruṣa because he lies in the city.”

justifications.decision: Do not read the speaker as merely begging a favor like a servant; the commentary explicitly rejects that framing before glossing so 'ham asmi by bhavāmi.
options_considered: a servant’s prayer for a vision only
an assertion of identity with that puruṣa
justifications.chosen: so 'ham asmi is an identity assertion: “that am I / I am he.”

evidence.translation: “Moreover, I do not beg you like a servant.”

translation:
O Pūṣan (nourisher), O ekarṣi (sole traverser), O Yama (restrainer), O Sūrya, O Prājāpatya (offspring of Prajāpati):
disperse your rays; draw together your scorching brilliance.
That form of yours which is most auspiciously beautiful—through your own favor—I behold.
That person (puruṣa) who is yonder, yonder in the solar disk: that am I.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering would likely translate ekarṣi as “one seer/sage”; Śaṅkara instead derives it from eka eva ṛṣati gacchati, “he alone goes.”
It might take vyūha as “arrange” the rays; the bhāṣya gloss vigamaya requires “disperse/remove.”
It might miss that tejaḥ is the accusative object of samūha and that the phrase means withdrawing the scorching light, not praising splendor in general.
It might take the final puruṣa as an ordinary “man”; the commentary locates him in the solar disk and reads the conclusion as identity, not mere servile petition.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 split ekarṣe into eka + ṛṣe; the printed mūla and the commentary’s “ityekarṣiḥ-- he ekarṣe” show a single vocative singular stem ekarṣi.
ByT5 gives prefixed verbal lemmas vyūh and samūh; following the required format, these are recorded as bare root ūh with prefixes vi and sam.
For tejaḥ I specify accusative singular, not merely the ambiguous neuter singular form, because the commentary glosses it as the object of samūha/upasaṃhara in line 2.
For both occurrences of te I specify genitive singular, following Śaṅkara’s gloss tava/tavātmanaḥ in line 3.
open_questions: Line 2 appears under-segmented: upasaṃharate tejastāpakaṃ is best read through the surface noise as upasaṃhara te tejas tāpakaṃ jyotiḥ; the apparatus cites the transmitted wording and flags the issue.

Line 4 contains unproofread-looking forms such as vyāhṛtyavayavaḥ and prāṇabuddhayātmanā; they are not needed for the core translation, so I rely only on the clear portions about the solar disk, puruṣa, and so 'ham asmi.
mula: pūṣann ekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ | yat te rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tat te paśyāmi yo 'sāv asau puruṣaḥ so 'ham asmi
